title: Microscope Slides in Motion — source and archive registry supplement 10

records.institution: University of St Andrews Libraries and Museums — Bell Pettigrew Zoology microscope-slide collection
records.collection: Charles Elcock Type Slides / Ostracoda group
records.type: distributed commercial Type Slide survival + item-level labels
records.date_scope: late nineteenth century; present institutional custody
records.holdings: St Andrews preserves six Charles Elcock slides together in sleeve 5/P/2. The collection record describes printed wording including TYPE SLIDE, SELECTED BY CHARLES ELCOCK, BELFAST and OSTRACODA, with manuscript specimen names. Recorded forms include Cythere darwini, C. goujoni, C. jonesii, C. scutigera, Cythere? from Hong Kong and C. convexa.
records.research_use: Independent institutional survival outside Elcock's retained Whipple workshop archive. These slides test how the Type Slide commercial format travelled, whether its printed matrix/list system was standardized across taxonomic groups, and how original product identities were absorbed into a later university teaching collection.
records.access: Online group/item records; physical research through St Andrews Libraries and Museums.

records.institution: University of St Andrews Libraries and Museums — Bell Pettigrew Zoology microscope-slide collection
records.collection: Stazione Zoologica Napoli / Fritz Meyer slides
records.type: historical commercial/institutional slide series + item-level labels
records.date_scope: late nineteenth century and later firm/preparator material
records.holdings: St Andrews preserves a named group of Stazione Zoologica Napoli slides, left in situ among the Bell Pettigrew sleeves. Group documentation links the slides to the Station's 423-offering catalogue and identifies Fritz Meyer as preparator of many surviving examples. Individual records preserve Stazione Zoologica or Fritz Meyer labels, subject wording and present/former pigeon-hole or sleeve addresses.
records.research_use: A surviving endpoint independent of the RMS shipment already reconstructed in the project. Item labels can be matched against the Naples catalogue and used to distinguish Station identity, Fritz Meyer preparator identity, later Leipzig Meyer labels, historical specimen wording and St Andrews re-addressing.
records.access: Online hierarchy and item records; research access through St Andrews Libraries and Museums.

records.institution: University of St Andrews Libraries and Museums — Bell Pettigrew Zoology microscope-slide collection
records.type: numbered specialist slide group + original boxes + dispersed collection route
records.date_scope: late nineteenth–early twentieth century Berlese collection context
records.holdings: Sixty-seven similarly mounted COLLEZIONI BERLESE slides survive upright in two wooden boxes in the Bell Pettigrew collection. Numbers in the boxes range from 37 to 194, and St Andrews suggests they correspond to a catalogue listing. Labels record Italian localities including Tuscany and Florence. One box is marked United Coll. Museum. CREA in Florence currently preserves and is actively valorising the principal Berlese Collection.
records.research_use: A compact test of how a numbered specialist collection became distributed across institutions. The immediate problem is to determine what the 37–194 numbers address, whether a historical catalogue/key survives in Florence, and how the St Andrews subset left the main Berlese collection.
records.access: St Andrews group/item records online; current Berlese Collection research route through CREA Difesa e Certificazione, Florence.

records.institution: Natural History Museum (formerly British Museum (Natural History))
records.collection: Heron-Allen & Earland Type Slide Collection of Foraminifera
records.type: indexed foraminiferal reference-slide collection + Keys + card index
records.date_scope: collection formed principally early twentieth century from material/practice rooted in the late nineteenth century; museum gifts 1926–1943
records.holdings: The institutional collection study documents 874 faunal Type Slides, generally addressed by TS numbers and supported by loose-leaf Keys and a card index. Internal squares are normally numbered. Some of the earliest slides are marked Charles Elcock, Belfast; the paper also records Elcock's gum-arabic/glycerine mounting treatment and notes Heron-Allen's personal connection with Elcock.
records.research_use: A powerful reference-archive comparator to Elcock's commercial Type Slides. It shows a later system in which Type Slide number, internal specimen fields, loose-leaf Keys and card index create a multi-layer retrieval architecture. The Elcock-labelled early slides create a documented bridge without proving direct invention/transmission of the format.
records.access: Published open collection study with collection description; object-level research through NHM micropalaeontology collections.
